info.title: Kast callable reference
info.description: Public compiler-grounded Kast callables invoked through the Kast CLI.

post.description:
Find named class-like declarations supported by Kast. This searches declaration names, not use sites or source text. Constructors are not included. Returns names, locations, signatures, opaque symbol references, and completeness evidence. Uses the session workspace's saved, indexed IntelliJ state; unavailable or unready hosts reject the read. No hidden fuzzy retry or scope widening.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Find named functions and methods. This searches declaration names, not call sites or source text. Returns every matching overload separately. Returns names, locations, signatures, opaque symbol references, and completeness evidence. Uses the session workspace's saved, indexed IntelliJ state; unavailable or unready hosts reject the read. No hidden fuzzy retry or scope widening.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Find named declarations when the kind is unknown or when searching properties or type aliases. Prefer search_classes or search_functions when that kind is known. Not a source-text or usage search. Returns names, locations, signatures, opaque symbol references, and completeness evidence. Uses the session workspace's saved, indexed IntelliJ state; unavailable or unready hosts reject the read. No hidden fuzzy retry or scope widening.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Advanced ordered symbol pipelines: search or enumerate declarations, start from returned references, filter visibility, expand semantic relations, and explicitly deduplicate. Prefer the dedicated search tools for ordinary name searches. Source restrictions do not constrain expansion destinations. Compiler identity, bounded work, and completeness remain owned by Kast. Does not accept diagnostic steps.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Find bounded Kotlin declaration candidates in the current workspace. Use when an exact selector is not already available. Returned candidate selectors are proof-carrying identities and must be preserved verbatim.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Refine a candidate into exact compiler-grounded symbol identity or inspect an existing exact selector. Prefer the returned exact selector over reconstructing symbol identity from source text.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Read bounded source and structural context around a candidate, exact symbol, or source selector. Prefer this over unrestricted filesystem reads when the required Kotlin context is representable through Kast.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Read one bounded compiler-grounded semantic relation from an exact selector. Use a Kast search tool first when exact identity is not established.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Perform bounded transitive semantic traversal from an exact selector. Required topology is acquired automatically for the current semantic state; the caller does not prepare it separately.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Check compiler diagnostics for a file or recursively beneath a directory in the session workspace. Use '.' explicitly for the workspace root. This is not symbol search and does not build the project. Results retain incomplete-coverage evidence; an incomplete empty result does not establish that the scope is clean. Requires the saved, indexed IntelliJ state.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Plan AddDeclaration in one existing authored Kotlin source file without writing source. Pass the returned search reference unchanged and preserve the plan identity for apply or recovery.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Apply one stored Kast plan with explicit approval of its exact identity. Verification is part of apply; preserve its verified receipt or qualified unverified/recovery state.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Recover one applied Kast change plan to a known workspace state. Requires explicit approval and the exact returned plan identity.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

class_name.description: Simple class-like declaration name, such as OrderService. Not a qualified name, signature, regex, glob, or natural-language request. Use package_name in scope for package qualification. All matching declarations remain separate results.

name_match.description: null means exact, case-sensitive declaration-name matching. Exact matching returns every matching overload; it does not select one overload. Fuzzy matching requires explicit opt-in.

scope.description: null searches the session workspace recursively in source sets main and test. Otherwise choose one directory scope or one package scope. Source-set restrictions intersect with the chosen scope.

relative_directory_path.description: Directory relative to the session workspace root, such as services/orders. Use '.' for the root. Not a file path, absolute path, glob, or package name. Parent traversal and non-canonical paths are rejected by server admission.

include_subdirectories.description: true includes the named directory and nested directories; false selects only the named directory.

items.description: Exact imported Gradle source-set name, such as main, integrationTest, or commonMain.

source_set_names.description: null selects the names main and test. Otherwise use exact imported Gradle source-set names, not paths, globs, or production/test categories. Empty and duplicate lists are rejected by server admission.

package_name.description: Semantic Kotlin package name, such as com.example.orders. Not a filesystem path. Uses Kast's supported package-name grammar.

include_subpackages.description: true includes the named package and subpackages; false selects only the named package.

steps.description: Ordered transformations, executed left to right. null and [] mean no transformations. Filtering before expansion and filtering after expansion have different meanings. Only the three advertised step shapes are supported; diagnostics are a separate tool.

return_fields.description: null returns name and location, [] requests mandatory identity and kind only. Symbol references and completeness evidence are always retained. Duplicate fields are rejected by server admission.

SearchSource.description: Find declarations and establish exact symbol identities. Source scope restricts discovery only, not later expansion destinations.

scope.description: null searches the session workspace recursively in source sets main and test. Otherwise choose one directory scope or one package scope. Source-set restrictions intersect with the chosen scope.

AllSource.description: Enumerate declarations under existing bounded execution. All does not mean unlimited work or guaranteed complete coverage.

items.description: Opaque exact-symbol reference returned by Kast. Copy the token verbatim; do not construct, edit, or substitute a candidate reference.

visibilities.description: Keep symbols with one of these compiler-established visibilities. Duplicate values are rejected by server admission.

relation.description: One semantic hop. callers means declarations calling the current symbols; callees means declarations called by them. This pipeline produces related symbols. Use the relation-read tool for occurrence-oriented relation facts.

DistinctSymbols.description: Remove duplicate symbol identities at this position only. Never insert this step implicitly.
